title: Expensive and Difficult to Access the Filter
text:
Expensive and Difficult to Access the Filter. I drink a lot of coffee and I have noticed the differences when coffee beans are fresh and when they go rancid. It's unpleasant, to say the least. I selected this container with the idea of keeping the coffee fresher longer. I have not had it long enough to know how effective it will be in the long run, but I do have some observations to share about it.

This is a stainless steel sealing jar with a latch lid and a silicone gasket to keep air out. I like the overall appearance and the feel of it. It comes with a little scoop too which is nice when you are using this jar to store grounds (not so much for whole beans). It has a nifty dial on the top that you can use to mark when you last filled the jar or when you need to empty it, as appropriate.

When I selected this jar I thought it would have a pump of some kind to extract air. That was my mistake. What this jar does is allow air out via a filter valve in the lid. That's fine and it is clear in the product description; it was my misunderstanding the design. Included are two extra filters.

I have two problems with this jar. First, it is expensive for what it is. Other similar steel jars are less expensive, which puts this one at a disadvantage. More importantly, though, it is unclear how to access the filter in the lid and as such there's no easy path for changing it. With no instructions in the box, I have not been able to figure out how to replace the filter that's installed prior to shipment. It looks like the cover holding it in place is supposed to twist to unlock, but it is so tight that I cannot get it to budge and I am unwilling to use tools for concern of damaging it.

I think this jar is a workable solution but there are a couple of things about it that give me some pause. The price is one, and the difficulty (?) of replacing the filter is another. If I figure out how to access the filter so it can be changed, I will will return here and update.
